transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because people keep telling me they can’t follow what I’m trying to explain. It's... it's affecting my work. 

My artist statements, my notes for clients, even just what I say in meetings—they've started jumping all over the place. I'll go from talking about the textures of a piece to suddenly bringing up budgets, and then getting into these secret meanings behind things. I know what I'm trying to say, but everyone else just says they can't understand me.
When did you first notice that people were having trouble following what you're saying? Was this something that started recently, or has this been a pattern throughout your life?

It's a more recent thing. I'd say this has been going on for about a year and two months. That's when I switched from doing community curation into full-time independent installation work. Before that, I didn't really have these issues with people not understanding me.

Over this past year, have you noticed changes in your mood or energy levels? For instance, have you been feeling particularly energized, optimistic, or on top of the world, or conversely, have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yeah, I have noticed some changes with my energy. For stretches of time, I'll feel totally lit up and almost unstoppable. It's like every idea I have is just brilliant. 

But... it's not always a good feeling. Sometimes, a really small comment from a collaborator can just make me snap. I get really irritable, in a way that definitely feels a lot bigger than the situation actually warrants.

You mentioned getting into 'secret meanings behind things' when you're talking—can you tell me more about what you mean by that? Are there hidden messages or special significance to things that you've been noticing?

Yeah, um, that's something that happens. I'll look at things—like a stain on the floor, or the way a seam is sewn on a canvas, or even just specific phrases in emails from galleries—and I get completely convinced that they're meant specifically for me. 

It feels like they're instructions, or maybe warnings about my work. And... it's really hard for me to let go of that idea. Even when a friend or a collaborator points out a totally ordinary explanation for it, I just can't shake the feeling that there's a message there just for me.

When you're feeling your normal mood—not particularly energized or irritable—do you still experience those feelings that things have hidden messages meant specifically for you, or do those only happen when your mood is elevated or when you're irritable?

Yeah, they do still happen. Actually, there was a... a quieter month recently where my mood felt pretty normal. I was sleeping better, not feeling so energized or unstoppable, just kind of baseline. But even during that time, for a few weeks, I was still reading those hidden warnings into just ordinary materials around the studio. And I'd still hear comments coming from behind the shelves, even when no one else was there. So, yeah, it doesn't just happen when my mood is up.
During that quieter month when your mood was baseline and stable, how long did those experiences of hearing comments from behind the shelves continue? Are they still happening now, or did they stop?

Well, um, during that quieter month... I guess it lasted for a few weeks. I was sleeping fine, not feeling all that energized or anything, but I was still hearing those comments from the shelves. And I was still seeing those warnings in the materials around the studio. It went on for a few weeks even though my mood was totally fine. They aren't happening right this second, but they definitely stuck around for a while during that baseline time.

When you're in one of those periods where you're feeling energized and everything seems brilliant, do the hidden messages and comments from the shelves get more intense or more frequent than they do during your normal baseline periods?

Yeah, they definitely happen then, too. Um, during my most charged-up work periods—like when I was sleeping very little and taking on way too much—I was also completely sure that the stains and the phrases in those emails were sending me instructions. And I would still sometimes hear that woman commenting in the studio. So, yeah, they are definitely still there when I have all that energy.

During that quieter month when your mood was baseline and stable, and you were still hearing those comments from the shelves—did you feel like those comments were connected to your mood at all, or did they feel completely separate from how you were feeling emotionally?

Um, they felt completely separate from my mood. Like I was saying before, there was that quieter month where I was sleeping more normally and I wasn't feeling unstoppable at all. My emotions were just... level. But even so, for several weeks during that time, I still kept hearing those comments from behind the shelves, and I was still reading hidden warnings into the ordinary materials around my studio. So, yeah, it really didn't seem connected to how I was feeling emotionally, because my mood was fine but those things were still happening anyway.

When you're having a conversation with someone, like right now with me, do you find it difficult to organize your thoughts and stay on one topic—or does the conversation flow pretty naturally for you most of the time?

Well, honestly, that's actually a big part of why I decided to come in. I've been having a really hard time keeping my thoughts straight. Like, when I'm writing artist statements or notes for clients, or even just talking in meetings... I end up jumping all over the place. I'll go from talking about the textures of the materials to the budget, and then suddenly I'm talking about those secret meanings I mentioned. People keep telling me they just can't follow what I'm trying to explain. It's really frustrating because in my head it all makes sense, but when it comes out, it's just a mess.
Right now, today, are you still hearing those comments from behind the shelves, or have they stopped completely?

Yeah, they haven't stopped. Even today, when I'm alone in the studio, I still sometimes hear that woman quietly commenting from behind the shelves. And occasionally, I'll also smell hot metal near an unfinished piece. It always feels completely real in the moment, but then I'll go check and there's absolutely nothing there. So, yes, it's still happening.

When you're hearing that woman's voice from behind the shelves or smelling the hot metal, do those experiences feel like they're happening because of your mood state at that moment, or do they feel like they're just happening on their own, completely independent of how you're feeling emotionally?

They definitely feel like they just happen on their own. Um, I think it's exactly like what I was mentioning earlier... even when I had that quieter month, where my sleep was totally normal and I didn't have that unstoppable energy at all, the things in the studio didn't stop. For several weeks during that really calm period, I was still hearing those comments from behind the shelves, and I was still reading those hidden warnings into just regular, ordinary materials around me. So, yeah, whether I'm feeling level or not, those experiences just seem completely independent of my mood.

Over the past few weeks, on how many days would you say you're hearing that woman's voice or experiencing those other perceptions in your studio? Is it happening every single day, or are there days when you don't experience them at all?

I'm not entirely sure on the exact number of days. I mean, it's not every single day, I don't think. There are definitely days when I don't notice the voice or the smells at all. But it's frequent enough that it's still a problem. Maybe a few times a week? It's hard to keep track of exactly how often it happens, to be honest.

You mentioned that during that quieter month, you were hearing the voice and seeing the warnings for a few weeks even though your mood was stable. During those few weeks when your mood felt normal and level, did the hearing of the voice and the seeing of those hidden warnings continue pretty much every day, or were there many days in that period when you didn't experience them at all?

Yeah, like I was saying before, during that quieter month when I was actually sleeping normally and not feeling all unstoppable, it was pretty constant. For those several weeks, it was basically every day. Even though I felt completely fine, I still kept hearing those comments from behind the shelves, and I was still reading hidden warnings into just ordinary studio materials. So even with my mood being totally level then, those things didn't really take a day off.

When you think back to that quieter month you described—the one where your sleep was normal and you weren't feeling that unstoppable energy—did your disorganized speech, the jumping around from topic to topic, get better during that time, or did that problem stay just as bad as it usually is?

Um, no, it didn't really get better. Actually, that jumping around is a big part of why I came in to get help in the first place. Even during that quiet month, people kept telling me they just couldn't follow what I was trying to explain. Like, whether I'm talking in meetings or writing out my artist statements and client notes, I'll start off on one thing and then just jump from, you know, textures... to budgets... and then right into those secret meanings. So, yeah, the trouble with getting my point across stayed just as bad.
